subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps
messages:

Date: 2026-08-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs - post-call recap

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

Summary of requirements you mentioned:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): p50 target ~150ms, p95 target <=400ms (you mentioned p95 is your blocking SLO)
- Throughput: steady-state ~50 requests/sec across your ingestion tier, with burst to 120 req/sec for 30s windows
- Concurrency: design for 200 concurrent streaming sessions
- Streaming: prefer WebSocket but SSE is acceptable; chunk cadence to support UI should be ~100–300ms between chunks
- Functionality: streaming partial tokens for UI (progressive rendering) + final completion integrity

Immediate next steps we agreed:
1) We’ll share a lightweight sample prompt set and an SLA draft (attached).
2) Redwood will run an internal perf baseline against a representative model variant and share TTFT/throughput numbers by EOD Friday.
3) Schedule a 30m follow-up with Redwood engineering to align on chunk cadence, backpressure, and retry behavior — suggested time: next Tue morning PT.

Attachments: SLA-Draft-EdgeRetail-v1.pdf, sample-prompt-set.csv

If any of the bullets above don’t match what you expect, flag them and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll coordinate the follow-up with Stephanie and Rishi.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa, appreciate the recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 
- Our product team would like p50 <=150ms and p95 <=350–400ms (we can tolerate up to 400ms p95 but prefer lower).
- For streaming transport, WebSocket is our first choice for lower-overhead bi-directional control; can you confirm Redwood supports WebSocket-based streaming SDK and whether it offers client backpressure control?
- Chunk cadence: our UI prefers chunks at ~120–250ms for smooth incremental rendering. Can you confirm practical limits (e.g., minimum chunk interval at scale)?
- Also please include a rough cost estimate for a trial (50 TPS average, 200 concurrent sessions) and whether a small dedicated pool is required to hit these TTFT numbers.

We’re aiming to have procurement and security questions addressed in parallel, so the SLA draft is helpful. Can we get an engineering follow-up early next week?

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs - post-call recap

Thanks — noted. Short answers while Stephanie and Rishi validate details: 
- Transport: Redwood supports both SSE and WebSocket streaming. We also have lightweight client SDKs that surface backpressure hooks for WebSocket (recommended for high-concurrency bi-directional control).
- Chunk cadence: recommended UI cadence is 120–300ms; practically we see reliable 100–150ms cadence in dedicated pools and ~200–300ms on multi-tenant hosted depending on load and model variant.
- Dedicated pool: for strict p95 targets under sustained concurrency, a small Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) is the most predictable path; we’ll outline cost/benefit in the perf note.

Stephanie / Rishi — can you confirm feasibility against EdgeRetail’s numbers (50 TPS steady, bursts to 120 TPS, 200 concurrent streaming sessions) and share a rough perf/cost estimate? Also any immediate red flags on chunk cadence or SDK behavior?

I’ll also propose 30m next Tue 10:30am PT for the technical follow-up — does that work for everyone?

Best,
Marissa
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@edgeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-14T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs - post-call recap (engineering note)

Hi Daniel — quick engineering note following Marissa’s recap: 

Short answers:
- TTFT targets: we can achieve p50 ~120ms and p95 ~350ms with a constrained model variant and a small Dedicated pool (N GPUs depending on model size). On multi-tenant hosted we typically see p95 400–600ms under 200 concurrent streaming sessions unless you pin capacity.
- Concurrency/Throughput: target profile (50 TPS steady, 120 TPS burst, 200 concurrent streams) is reasonable. We recommend a small dedicated capacity configuration to keep tail latency low during bursts.
- Streaming transport & backpressure: WebSocket is preferred for EdgeRetail’s flow — it provides lower protocol overhead and stronger backpressure semantics. Our streaming SDK exposes an onChunk callback and allows client-side buffer limits; server-side we expose chunk-size and flush cadence knobs.
- Chunk cadence guidance: aim for 120–250ms for best UX. Very low chunk intervals (<50ms) increase overhead and can actually worsen throughput; >400ms can feel choppy.

Action items we’ll take this week:
1) Run a targeted benchmark using your sample prompt set and report TTFT p50/p95, throughput, and median chunk latency (attached).
2) Provide a cost estimate for a 2-week trial on a small Dedicated pool that meets the targets.
3) Draft recommended client SDK settings and a quick integration checklist (SSE vs WS snippets, reconnection/backoff guidance).

I attached a small perf extract (ttft-benchmarks-rt1.csv) and will follow up with the benchmark report by EOD Friday. If you’re available, the suggested Tue 10:30am PT follow-up works for me.

—Stephanie
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
